newsitem.title: USA: Volvo boosts stake in U.S. truck unit.
newsitem.headline: Volvo boosts stake in U.S. truck unit.

text.p: Swedish automaker AB AB Volvo has increased its investment in Volvo GM Heavy Truck Corp and will change the U.S. truck venture's name to Volvo Trucks North America, Volvo Trucks said Wednesday.
Volvo Trucks' Canadian affiliate also will eliminate GM from its name.
Volvo Trucks said the agreement to increase its investment was made between General Motors Corp and the parent of Volvo Trucks, Volvo Truck Corp of Gothenburg, Sweden, a unit of AB Volvo.
Terms of the agreement were not disclosed.
A Volvo Trucks spokesman in North Carolina, reached later, said Volvo has acquired 100 percent of the truck maker's common stock. Most recently, GM had owned 13 percent of Volvo GM Heavy Truck.
GM will retain one seat on the unit's board of directors, the spokesman said.
"We are now Volvo," said Marc Gustafson, President and CEO of Volvo Trucks, said in a statement. "This investment is a concrete sign of Volvo's commitment to the North American truck market."

"Volvo Trucks is poised to build a stronger organization which will enable it to achieve the same level of success as its parent has in other parts of the world," he added. "We will grow to become one of the top OEMs in the North American marketplace."

Volvo entered the U.S. heavy truck market in 1981 when it purchased assets of the White Motor Co. In 1988, it combined those assets with GM's heavy truck business, creating Volvo GM Heavy Truck Corp, at the time 76 percent owned by Volvo and 24 percent by GM.
The companies marketed trucks under the White-GMC name until 1995, when it switched to the Volvo name on all of its products.
